entry.name: scale~
entry.digest: Map an input range of signal values to an output range
entry.description: Use the scale~ object to map an input range of signal values to an output range. The ranges can be specified with hi and lo reversed for inverted mapping. If specified, the mapping can also be exponential.

arguments.name: minimum-in-value
arguments.description: The first argument is the minimum input value used in the scaling operation.

arguments.name: maximum-in-value
arguments.description: The second argument is the maximum input value used in the scaling operation.

arguments.name: minimum-out-value
arguments.description: The third argument is the minimum output value used in the scaling operation.

arguments.name: maximum-out-value
arguments.description: The fourth argument is the maximum output value used in the scaling operation.

arguments.name: scaling-curve
arguments.description: This optional fifth argument specifies the nature of the scaling curve. This argument must be a floating-point number greater than 1., with larger values leading to steeper exponential curves.Inmode a typical value for this argument is 1.06 and the number is converted according to the following expression:(out_high-out_low >= 0) ? (out_low + (out_high-out_low) * ( (out_high - out_low) * exp(-1*(in_high-in_low)*log(power)) * exp(x*log(power)) )) : (-1) * ( out_low + (out_high-out_low) * ( (out_high - out_low) * exp(-1*(in_high-in_low)*log(power)) * exp(x*log(power)) ) )In non-(modern) mode the value for the scaling curve must be higher than 0. and is converted according to the following expression:((x-in_low)/(in_high-in_low) == 0) ? out_low : (((x-in_low)/(in_high-in_low)) > 0) ? (out_low + (out_high-out_low) * ((x-in_low)/(in_high-in_low))^exp) : ( out_low + (out_high-out_low) * -((((-x+in_low)/(in_high-in_low)))^(exp)))Note that prior to Max 6.0.4 the exponent was inverted. Thus, if you gave it an exponent of 2 the object behaved like it had an exponent of 0.5, and if you gave it an exponent of 0.5 it behaved like it had an exponent of 2. Patches from versions prior to 6.0.4 may require updating to work properly.

attributes.name: classic
attributes.digest: Backward compatibility mode
attributes.description: Classic mode uses exponential function that is backward compatible with old IRCAM patchers.

choices.label: Whenis 0,applies an exponential (power) function after scaling the input to be between 0 and 1, then scales the resulting output.
Whenis 1,is compatible with legacy IRCAM "linedrive" scaling. This mode is not recommended for new work.

Whenis 2,operates similarly to0, except that when the output range inverts the value -- in other words, when the first output value is greater than the second output value -- the exponential is also inverted so that the scaling curve retains the shape produced by the non-inverted output range.
